parsed.explanation: Under the combined national-state regime, a trans visitor faces severe federal-facing exposure at entry: passport/visa marker rules, sex-doubt refusal, permanent-fraud ineligibility, reports of passports confiscated and foreign advisories. If outed in custody, documented immigration/federal detention harms and birth-sex facility arrest/warding raise severity. Many national/state facility restrictions criminalize congruent facility use; official counterterrorism language treats radical pro-transgender ideology as a threat. The division's anti-discrimination commission, low-risk status, marker flexibility, and sanctuary-city care shield are real but local and cannot cancel federal border screening, facilities, custody, or immigration fraud. For an adult with a minor, care/school exposure is heightened by national hostility to youth transition. Net: High Risk, below border-only 0.35 anchors, above 0.15 due no routine capital or long prison.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented visa/border sex-doubt screening: mismatched passports, names, or presentation can trigger refusal, additional evidence, permanent fraud ineligibility, passport block/confiscation, stranding, and foreign advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Partial: lawsuits, legal-aid FAQ, and existing X passports valid until expiration. No documented reliable traveler remedy at inspection.
entry_documents.interaction: Border doubt can feed detention, removal, and later facility or care exposure; state and city rules cannot offset inspection.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented federal immigration and custody harms: forced labor, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse, conversion-therapy rules, denial of care; one bathroom arrest led to men's ward detention.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts and national hate-crime law exist, but not shown to prevent federal birth-sex placement or immigration abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody consequences follow entry screening, facility arrests, or care disputes and override local mitigations.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Documented national ban on congruent use in government-funded single-sex spaces; many state bans, including criminal trespass and private-setting bans; one arrest and 24-hour detention.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The rated state is low-risk, has no mapped facility ban, and the largest city mandates gender-neutral public-building bathrooms.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State and city protections do not cover federal buildings or land; visitor facility use remains risk-graded by location.

care_services.exposure: Documented national hostility to youth care and education, funding freezes, proposed insurance bars, records subpoenas, and removed LGBTQ crisis services; adult care access is uncertain under national orders.
care_services.protection: State permits adult gender-affirming surgery and no adult care ban appears; largest city sanctuary order shields care-seeking travelers from external enforcement.
care_services.interaction: City sanctuary may reduce local care exposure, but cannot cancel federal funding, interstate travel consequences, or other jurisdictions.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism language prioritizes neutralizing radically pro-transgender groups and federal guidance references radical gender ideology; enforcement produced bathroom arrests and men's ward placement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State commission investigates discrimination and awards remedies; city deprioritizes enforcement against trans people and care seekers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing raises policing and custody severity even where street violence is not campaign-scale.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor or guardian can face school or health investigations under national orders, care restrictions, opt-out rulings, and document-marker scrutiny; parent mismatched travel papers may create fraud or permanent ineligibility exposure.
minors_guardians.protection: State allows birth-certificate marker changes with physician and parent request; city sanctuary for care; no local adult care ban documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family trips amplify document and care-check exposure; national anti-minor framing can escalate local friction into custody or care denial.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented social hostility and public opinion; potential police stops, ejection, or arrest under facility rules; no statewide anti-LGBTQ hate-crime statute in the rated state.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National, state, and city discrimination protections and commission remedies; police behavior in low-risk state may be less targeting, but unproven for visitors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street friction can become police contact if facilities, events, or care disputes draw attention; local remedies are uneven.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unresolved litigation, pending bills, variable enforcement, opaque visa and fraud standards, and limited permanent-ineligibility waivers create unpredictable stranding or detention outcomes.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ, lawsuits, state commission; no documented fast traveler-specific remedy that reliably reverses detention or entry refusal.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist at some levels but not for the operative federal entry, facility, and custody path.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar severe document and custody abuse plus state hostility, but this jurisdiction lacks routine long pretrial custody for mere presentation and includes state and city anti-discrimination protections; score modestly above 0.15.

0.35-A exposure is exclusion and humiliation without imprisonment; this adds immigration forced labor and sexual abuse, facility arrest, permanent-fraud and counterterrorism framing, so materially below 0.35.
Comparable birth-sex custody and facility arrest plus slow remedies; low-risk state protections and sanctuary city lift it above 0.25-C, while federal entry and custody keep it below upper High Risk.

parsed.synthesis: Federal screening, document mismatch, and facility bans make discovery consequential; state and city anti-discrimination and sanctuary care reduce some local exposure but cannot cancel border, federal facilities, immigration or federal custody, or counterterrorism threats. Adult alone: possible refusal, stranding, arrest in hostile facilities, severe detention if discovered. With minor: school and care hostility adds pressure. Net: High Risk due universal federal-facing exposures, partially mitigated locally.
